articleTitle: Dispersion and nonlinearity compensation using electronic predistortion techniques
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: The development of CMOS-based digital signal processors, A/D and D/A converters operating at rates exceeding 20 GSa/s is enabling advances in the performance of electronic techniques to mitigate optical transmission impairments at bit-rates of 10 Gb/s and above. Digital processing techniques can be used to overcome signal distortion caused by fibre dispersion and nonlinearity, polarization mode dispersion, WDM crosstalk, and optical and electrical filtering. In this paper, recent advances in the use of signal predistortion using DSP are described, and results of simulations of long-haul 10 Gb/s transmission, investigating simultaneous compensation of chromatic dispersion and intra-channel nonlinearity are presented. Practical digital filter architectures are proposed to achieve nonlinear compensation

articleTitle: Comparison of optical and electronic dispersion compensation strategies
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: This paper discusses the comparison of optical and electronic dispersion compensation on system architecture, economic and performance analysis. Performance impact of fibre nonlinearities is presented

articleTitle: Differential quadrature phase shift keying with close to homodyne performance based on multi-symbol phase estimation
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: We discuss an improved detection scheme for differential phase shift keying (DPSK) and differential quadrature phase shift keying (DQPSK), based on multi-symbol phase estimation (MSPE) through electrical signal processing. Using a recursive electrical signal processing algorithm, close to homodyne performance is obtained without a local oscillator at the receiver. In the presence of only Gaussian noise the proposed scheme yields a 0.5 dB and 1.8 dB sensitivity improvement over self-homodyne detection, for DPSK and DQPSK respectively. It furthermore improves robustness against impairments due to the influence of a finite laser linewidth and nonlinear phase noise

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion compensation employing optical all pass filter by using IIR structure for 10Gb/s optical communication systems
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: In current high bit rate long haul point to point optical communication system, the chromatic dispersion of a single mode fibre is the main limitation to increase the bit rate. This paper proposes a promising technique to compensate chromatic dispersion, hence improving the bit error rate and repeater-less span. This compensation scheme uses an optical all pass filter equaliser that is optimised by minimum mean square error technique. The practical implementation of an optical all pass filter using passive infinite impulse response digital filter structure is also introduced. The simulated results showed that a dispersed rectangular pulse is fully compensated at full-width half at maximum after propagating 160 km of SMF and the resultant eye pattern showed an improvement to the bit error rate when the proposed optical all pass filter equaliser is used

articleTitle: Robust optical systems using maximum likelihood sequence estimators
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: We examine the use of maximum likelihood sequence estimators (MLSE) in realising robust optical transmission systems. Such systems will be more tolerant to non-ideal installations in which, for example, the residual dispersion, or the launch power, are not at the optimum level. We present experimental results for 10 Gb/s transmission, assessing the enhancement in tolerance to chromatic dispersion and launch power through the use of MLSE

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of optical communication systems using extreme value theory
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: In this paper, a performance estimation scheme based on the extreme value theory is applied to the optical communications for the first time. The results are promising compared with those obtained be the standard Gaussian approximation method and the multicanonical Monte Carlo method

articleTitle: High capacity transmission of adaptively modulated optical ofdm signals over multimode fibres using directly modulated dfbs
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: Numerical simulations of the transmission performance of a recently proposed optical signal modulation technique, adaptively modulated optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (AMOOFDM), are undertaken in un-amplified multi-mode fibre (MMF)-based links using directly modulated DFB lasers (DMLs). It is shown that 28 Gb/s over 300 m and 10 Gb/s over 900 m transmission of intensity-modulation and direct-detection (IMDD) AMOOFDM signals at 1550 nm is feasible in DML-based links using MMFs with 3-dB effective bandwidths of as small as 150 MHz.km. Apart from a higher signal transmission capacity, AMOOFDM also has a greater spectral efficiency and is less susceptible to different launching conditions, modal dispersion and fibre types, compared with all existing schemes. In addition, a large noise margin of about 15 dB is also observed. The bits of resolution of analogue-to-digital converters and the cyclic prefix of AMOOFDM symbols are the main factors limiting the maximum achievable performance, on which the influence of DMLs is, however, negligible under the optimum operating condition

articleTitle: BER estimation of a MLSE using the union bound
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: A lower bound and the union upper bound of the bit error rate (BER) of the maximum-likelihood (ML) receiver of an optical on/off-keying (OOK) system is derived in this paper. Combining the two bounds, the BER of the ML receiver can be estimated

articleTitle: Low-cost receiver side electronic dispersion compensation of the full optical field
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: We propose a novel electronic dispersion compensation technique utilising a simple receiver configuration and a conventional transmitter that allows 10.7 Gbit/s transmission over 600 km of standard single-mode fibre

articleTitle: Electronic suppression of the four wave mixing-induced distortion in WDM optical communication systems
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: In this paper, an initial discussion is presented on the potential of applying electronic equalization in WDM optical communication systems. The novelty of our work is that the fibre is considered nonlinear with FWM being the dominant source of distortion. Possible dependencies between the outputs of the desired channel and the bits transmitted in other channels are explored and some simple joint channel equalization structures are tested

articleTitle: All-optical packet header processing scheme based on pulse position modulation in packet-switched networks
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate all-optical ultrafast pulse-position-modulation (PPM) based header processing scheme for all-optical packet-switched network with up to 32 nodes by means of software simulation. A new routing table and packet header address format based on PPM is proposed, which offers reduced routing table size and the header-processing time. In addition, we show that packet forwarding in multiple transmitting modes is also possible. Simulation results presented demonstrate the working principal of the proposed concept

articleTitle: Characterisation of multimode fibre links for 10 Gb/s optical communications utilising electronic dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: A set of multimode fibers have been created that in combination with launch and offset patchcords comprise a set of reference links. Several techniques for characterizing the links have been employed, each bringing unique insights to the nature of the link responses. By considering the results of each of the measurements, a better understanding of the type of stress that a links presents to an adaptive equalizer is achieved. Finally, a method to reduce the error in these measurements has been employed in practice

articleTitle: Modelling of EDC-enabled multimode fibre links
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: The application of electronic dispersion compensation (EDC) technology to extended-reach operation of multimode-fibre (MMF) links is considered. The essential theory is described in the context of MMF and the application of statistical techniques to predict supported link lengths for EDC-enabled MMF links is presented

articleTitle: Potential benefit of using electronic equalisation in all-optical networks
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: All-optical network is the potential candidate for next generation optical networks. In addition to its potential CAPEX and OPEX savings compared with the current OEO type of optical networks, it also imposes significant technical challenges due to its transparency. In this paper, we look into application of the emerging techniques such as electronic equalisation in the transparent optical networks, showing potential benefit of electronic signal processing in improving transmission performance, network simplification and cost reduction

articleTitle: Digital equalisation at 10.7Gb/s using maximum likelihood sequence estimation- a present and future technology
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: Improvements in silicon processing speeds have resulted in integrated circuits that can sample and digitally process 10 Gbit/s data. Signal processing techniques that have radically altered radio communication can now be applied to optical communications to improve tolerance to impairments such as chromatic dispersion and polarisation mode dispersion, as well as transmitter/receiver imperfections. Whereas optical components tend to be expensive to produce, electronics lends itself to integration and mass production, leading to a reduction in network level cost. For low cost systems using direct detection at the receiver, maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) is recognised as being the optimum receiver detection method. We present architecture & results from our first generation digital equaliser chip set (DECS). The equaliser requires no previous knowledge of the transmission channel, can adapt to channel changes, is robust against transient behaviour, and has been demonstrated in conjunction with NRZ. The MLSE algorithm may also be used in conjunction with other technologies such as duobinary or directly-modulated lasers to further increase the tolerance to signal distortion and therefore reduce the network cost. We discuss the challenges in a practical implementation of the MLSE

articleTitle: A first demonstrator for a mode group diversity multiplexing communication system
publicationTitle: The 2005 IEE Seminar on Optical Fibre Communications and Electronic Signal Processing (Ref. No. 2005-11310)
abstract: This paper describes a first demonstration setup for the transparent transmission of two analog signals using mode group diversity multiplexing (MGDM). MGDM is an optical multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique suitable for short-reach multimode fibre networks. In this demonstrator two baseband analog signals are transmitted together with out-of-band pilot tones. Measurements of the pilot tones are used at the receiver to estimate the transmission matrix; the inverse of this matrix is then used to demultiplex the received signals. A number of experimental results are given for the performance of the experimental setup
